conditions.detail: Only the recipe's own SGLang container (qwen3.8-27b-sglang) was resident; nothing else used the GPU.
conditions.isolation_check: docker ps -> qwen3.8-27b-sglang dgx-exporter ; nvidia-smi compute apps -> 2; load1 at start 1.06

gotchas.text: No engine version file for sglang@0.0.0.dev1+g5f55db35e; no defaults could be dropped from the canonical config.

Boot lottery: this boot allocated the KV pool at the recipe-capped max-total-tokens of 1,048,576 (target cache torch.float8_e4m3fn, K 16.00 GB + V 16.00 GB; the DFlash2 draft cache is the same dtype at K 5.00 GB + V 5.00 GB), with mem-fraction-static 0.85 and the native 262144 window, leaving 17.13 GB free after CUDA-graph capture. The recipe documents boot-to-boot variance of about 8 percent on single-stream against under 2 percent run-to-run inside one server instance, so read a pool number out of the log of the boot it belongs to and size any A/B delta against 8 percent.

Five mamba state slots per request, not four. SGLang clamps max_running_requests to max_mamba_cache_size divided by 5, so the recipe sizes the GDN pool at 80 for a target of 16. That held here: the server log reports max_running_requests=16 with no clamp line, which is the check the recipe asks for after any change to either flag.

The GDN state pool costs more on this image than the recipe measured. At the same 80 slots with --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 the server allocated conv_state 0.22 GB + ssm_state 5.70 GB + intermediate_ssm_state_cache 19.12 GB + intermediate_conv_window_cache 0.28 GB, so 25.3 GB against the 15.6 GB in the recipe memory table, and 17.13 GB free after load against its 20.6 GB. The recipe numbers came from a locally built image on an older SGLang; this ran the official lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13-qwen38-27b-dflash2, engine version 0.0.0.dev1+g5f55db35e. Budget the difference before raising the pool to the 160 the recipe calls the practical ceiling.

The recipe fetch script downloads both checkpoints into the real ~/.cache/huggingface, but the toolkit launcher it hands off to sets HF_HOME to the working directory it is started from, so following the two documented steps in order re-downloads about 25 GB into the toolkit directory. The weights were staged across as hardlinks instead. Hardlinks are safe here; symlinks are not, because the container bind-mounts that directory and an in-mount symlink to a host-only path makes it re-download and then fail with OSError File exists.

A download pinned to a revision leaves no refs/main in the Hugging Face cache, and SGLang resolves the draft config in its early speculative-algorithm probe without a revision. refs/main was written for both repositories before the first start, pointing at the pinned snapshots, so the probe resolved locally and the server log shows no lookup for either.

The toolkit launcher builds its command line for EAGLE and the DFlash2 wrapper only appends overrides, so --speculative-num-steps 3 and --speculative-eagle-topk 1 are still on the command line under --speculative-algorithm DFLASH. SGLang resolved speculative_num_steps to 1 for DFlash2 and ignored the rest; the served args record what the server parsed, not what the wrapper passed.

Draft tokens are set to 16, the recipe README step 6 optimum for interactive single-stream work. The recipe is explicit that the optima diverge and that 10 is the better setting for concurrent serving, worth 435 against 385 aggregate tok/s in its own sweep, so the c8 and c16 rows here are measured at the single-stream setting and are not this recipe at its concurrency optimum.

This is the standalone launch path of README step 3 plus the step 5 and step 6 tuning passed through DF_EXTRA, not the SparkStation orchestration of step 4. The recipe measures the LiteLLM gateway overhead at zero (62.3 against 62.5 tok/s), and its own traps list the SparkStation supervisor restarting a healthy model mid-job when a long prefill cannot answer a 5 second health probe, which would corrupt the long-context rows. No systemd unit, supervisor or cockpit was installed.

The server runs with no API key and with sleep_on_idle false, so unlike some recipes on this cell there is no idle wake-up cost on the first request after a gap. Every workload still ran after a warm-up request on an already-answering server.

Target revision 554ebba9 is the same revision the atlas quant entry nvfp4-fp4-lmhead pins, so no revision patch was needed. Passing it is still required: the recipe warns that downloading the right checkpoint does not make SGLang load it, and --revision has to be given to the server separately.

Speed rows force thinking off per request with chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking false. Eval rows use the served default, which here is thinking on at full length, because the chat template comes from the target repository unmodified and sampling-defaults is model. The recipe warns that a small token cap with thinking on returns empty content with everything in reasoning_content, which reads as a quality regression: it scored one of its own 97.0 percent runs at 90.9 percent that way.

provenance.notes: Served with the darkdatter DGX Spark Qwen3.8-27B recipe (https://github.com/darkdatter/gb10-repo, main 2db1ecd), using its standalone README step 3 path rather than the SparkStation orchestration of step 4: ./scripts/01-build-and-fetch.sh pulled the official LMSYS image lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13-qwen38-27b-dflash2 and both pinned checkpoints, then the recipe-pinned MiaAI-Lab toolkit (Qwen3.8-27B-SGLang-DGX-Spark at c90d8c34) launched the server with IMAGE set and DF_EXTRA carrying the recipe tuning. Target RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 at revision 554ebba9, DFlash2 speculative decoding against z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 at revision 50307d4c with 16 draft tokens (the README step 6 interactive optimum), mem-fraction-static 0.85, max-total-tokens capped at 1048576, the README step 5 concurrency trio max-running-requests 16 with max-mamba-cache-size 80 and cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16, KV cache fp8_e4m3, bf16 mamba SSM state, mamba radix cache extra_buffer, FlashInfer attention with autotune left on, chunked prefill 8192, prefill CUDA graph off, torch.compile off, and the native 262144 context window. The container is CPU-pinned to the GB10 Cortex-X5 cores 5-9,15-19 by the toolkit launcher. The chat template comes from the target repository, reasoning-parser qwen3 and sampling-defaults model, so the served default is thinking on: the speed rows force thinking off per request with chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking false, the eval rows use that served default. The server runs without an API key; the harness attached over HTTP on 127.0.0.1:8888 and sent a bearer header the server ignores. No systemd unit, no SparkStation supervisor and no cockpit were installed.
